title: shared shapes
description: The shapes mankit gives every Go app, written once and referenced with $ref, so each app's answers describe them in one place. The document itself takes one of each, so its sample shows them.

featureState.description: One feature an app can switch, and whether it is on on this machine: mankit's features.State, which every Go app answers its switches with.

id.description: The feature's id, which the app's enable feature and disable feature take.

covers.description: What the feature covers, in words for people, so a reader says what switching it off closes.

needs.description: The values the feature needs to run, so switching it on can name each one missing; absent when it needs none.

startsOff.description: True for a feature that is off until switched on, so a reader says why it is off on a new machine; absent when it starts on.

on.description: True when nothing closes the feature, so its routes and controls are open.

by.description: What closed it; absent while it is on. An open word, so a later closer (public mode, a license) needs no new contract, and a reader shows the words for any other. Known words: switch: the owner switched it off; default: it starts off and nobody switched it on.

missing.description: The values the feature needs that are not set, so a feature that is on but cannot run says why; absent when none is missing.

featureValue.description: One value a feature needs, such as an environment variable or a settings row: mankit's features.Value.

name.description: The value's name, as it is set.

purpose.description: What the feature needs it for, in words for people.

storeKey.description: A thing's key in mankit's store: a slash path inside the store's scope, never a machine path (ADR-S21, S22), so nothing named by a key reaches outside the scope. Each thing has one key: the store normalises a key before using it, so a key it writes is never in another form, with no . or .. step, no empty step (no leading, trailing or doubled slash) and no backslash; and no drive letter or scheme such as file:, no leading ~ and no leading space, which would read as a machine path; so a key's first step holds no colon after its leading letters, as C:shop or file:shop would name a place outside the scope.

storeUnfinishedChange.description: One change cut short, as <app> store unfinished list and clear show it: mankit's store.Unfinished. A change with a mark holds its keys back until its user's next run puts it back or a person clears the mark; a left journal is this user's journal whose marks are gone, kept as the only copy of what was there (ADR-S22, store-unfinished.schema.json).

id.description: The mark's id, the same in every .queue/ folder the change marked, so a person names one change whichever thing they look at.

user.description: The user whose journal holds the change, so a person knows who must run the app again to put it back.

host.description: The machine the journal is on, so a person knows where that run must be.

journal.description: The id of the journal that holds the change (a StoreJournal's metadata.id).

folder.description: true when the change also holds the served folder's own turn: a change to the scope itself, or one that adds a thing, or moves or removes the thing itself, so changes to the folder itself wait too. Left out when false.

keys.description: Every key the change writes, so a person sees what it holds back; never empty for a change whose mark is there. A left journal names the keys of its lines, none when it was cut short before its first line was written: it still shows, as a file a person may look at and remove.

file.description: The journal's file on this machine, only when it is this user's and still there, so a person can look at what was there before clearing the mark or putting it back by hand; always there for a left journal, which is one of this user's files. A machine path, shown to a person only, never a key.

left.description: true for a journal of this user's whose marks are gone, cleared or lost: it holds nothing back and puts nothing back by itself, and stays as the only copy of what was there. Left out for a change whose mark is there.

allOf.description: A left journal is this user's file on this machine, so it always names it.
A change whose mark is there holds at least one key, as its mark does (store-unfinished.schema.json).
